target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`. A slow drip resets the per-chunk idle timer on every chunk, so the existing 300s byte-idle budget never fires.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, the response timer is cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remains. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets only when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases. Status-only post-download finalization gets **one non-renewable grace arm**; further status-only lines (including distinct novel freeform statuses) cannot renew it, so:

- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy finite finalization phases survive inside one grace window
- cycling or novel status drips without completed progress cannot act as an unlimited keepalive

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

Collision check: searched open and closed PRs for `ollama pull stream watchdog`, `ollama pull no-progress`, `ollama setup pull`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found. The closest closed PR (#99585) bounds native streaming body size, not progress.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping `/api/pull` stream fails closed with a no-progress error. Healthy pulls that keep advancing `completed` survive. Finite status-only finalization survives within one grace budget. Distinct novel status drips without completed progress are bounded - removing the prior availability hang bypass.

## Evidence

Exact head: `e5865eb6a3f859380749daefb6f0e88b9f68a435`

`oxfmt --check extensions/ollama/src/{setup.ts,setup.test.ts,setup.test-helpers.ts,setup.pull.test.ts,setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts}` - passed; exit 0.
`git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.

### Real behavior proof

Loopback HTTP server (`http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1`) simulates Ollama `/api/pull` NDJSON behaviors. The production function `ensureOllamaModelPulled` (no mocked fetch - real `fetch` against the loopback server) is exercised across all four adversarial scenarios plus the two healthy paths.

Quantified results from the loopback suite (streamNoProgressTimeoutMs=250, streamIdleTimeoutMs=10_000 unless noted):

| Scenario | Server behavior | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle drip never settles | 40ms interval `pulling manifest` status-only drip; `streamIdleTimeoutMs=100`, `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs=1500` | Still pending at 500ms; then rejected by no-progress | Settled=false at 500ms; rejected with `WizardCancelledError` containing "no progress for" |
| Non-advancing drip abort | 40ms interval `pulling manifest` status-only drip | Reject within 250ms budget | 310ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Finite status-only finalization grace | 5 advancing chunks then 5 distinct status phases (`verifying sha256 digest`, `writing manifest`, `pulling manifest`, `checking blob`, `cleanup`) then `success` | Complete inside one 150ms grace | 178ms elapsed; `Downloaded gemma4`; no "no progress for" |
| Distinct novel status drip abort | 40ms interval `stalled phase N` for N=0,1,2,… | Reject within 250ms budget | 307ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Cycling status drip abort | 40ms interval alternating `verifying sha256 digest` / `writing manifest` | Reject within 250ms budget (one grace only) | 312ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Advancing completed succeeds | 80ms interval `completed += 250` up to 2000 then `success` | Complete past 250ms no-progress window | 650ms elapsed; `Downloaded gemma4`; no "no progress for" |

Loopback server sources: `extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts` - real `node:http`, real `fetch`, real `ReadableStream` consumer inside `pullOllamaModelCore`.

### Mutation checks

```bash
# 1. Fix in place: loopback suite passes
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> Tests 6 passed (6), Duration 8.65s

# 2. Revert setup.ts to origin/main and rerun loopback suite
cp extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts /tmp/setup.ts.fixed
git show origin/main:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts > extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts
timeout 25 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> timeout exit=124; suite hangs because no-progress watchdog is absent;
#    the drip server keeps the per-chunk idle timer resetting forever.

# 3. Restore fix and rerun
cp /tmp/setup.ts.fixed extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> Tests 6 passed (6), Duration 8.65s
```

### Not tested

- No live local Ollama daemon pull was run. The loopback suite exercises the real production `pullOllamaModelCore` fetch/ReadableStream path against a local `node:http` server that replays the same NDJSON shapes Ollama emits, so transport and parser behavior are covered, but production server timing cadence (e.g. very long status-only finalization phases) is not observed against a real `ollama serve` instance.
- Provider auth, OAuth, push surfaces, iOS/Android native: not touched by this change.
- The two optional timeout parameters on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are test-only knobs; production callers do not pass them and inherit the 300s default.
